title: Strict quotient balancing and pullback preserve the quotient augmentation
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For a scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_T$, $\underline{P_n}_T$, and $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$, with canonical scalar map $\underline A_T\to A_T$ and quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All sites are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(A_T)$ and $D(\underline A_T)$ for unbounded derived module categories and $r_T$ for restriction along this scalar map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, $\Delta$ be its constant-diagram functor, and $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions. On the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], define $\mathcal R_T^aL=\Delta L\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_T$ and $\mathcal R_T^0L_0=\Delta L_0\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}Q_T$. These are actual derived strict towers. For an edge $u:U\to V$ use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$, $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], the ordinary ringed operations $L_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], their strict-diagram operations $\mathscr L_u^a\dashv\mathscr R_u^a$, and the constant-coefficient counterparts $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $a_u:r_UL_u^a\cong G_ur_V$, $\chi_u:r_VR_u^a\cong R_u^0r_U$, $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u^a\cong G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^a\cong R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$ be the normalized flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

For every ambient $L\in D(A_T)$ there is a natural strict-diagram balancing isomorphism $\rho_L:r_T\mathcal R_T^aL\cong\mathcal R_T^0r_TL$. On a flat-term K-flat representative it is the balancing map identifying the two quotient diagrams, sending each tensor class to itself, with all quotient transitions. It satisfies the strict augmentation equation $\rho_Lr_T(\Delta L\to\mathcal R_T^aL)=(\Delta r_TL\to\mathcal R_T^0r_TL)$ under $r_T\Delta\cong\Delta r_T$. Here K-flat means tensoring with the complex takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $\tau_{u,L}:\mathcal R_U^aL_u^aL\cong\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL$ be canonical pullback/tensor reassociation [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Set $q_{u,L}=(G_u\rho_L)p_{u,\mathcal R_V^aL}$. Then
$$q_{u,L}\,r_U(\tau_{u,L})=\mathcal R_U^0(a_{u,L})\rho_{L_u^aL},$$
where the right side uses the canonical identification $\mathcal R_U^0G_u\cong G_u\mathcal R_V^0$.

All these are natural isomorphisms and equalities in the actual derived strict-tower category, on arbitrary ambient inputs.

proof.text: Use derivedReductionTowerComparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and invert its comparison. Its representative formula is exactly BalancingComputes. All data and predicates are those of [def-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing-data].

Lift the exact constant-diagram restriction square through the localization of complexes. Define the quotient augmentation by the universal left-derived lift of the ordinary reductionUnit; the Kan factorization equation proves AugmentationComputes on every complex. These use the exact restriction and universal quotient presentations of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

Before localization, both reduction units send m to 1 tensor m. The finiteComparison and reductionTowerComparison section specifications therefore give equality of the ordinary augmented strict towers. Choose a flat-term K-flat completed-coefficient resolution by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Flatness of the coefficient map from [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-restriction-kflat] keep its restriction K-flat with flat terms. The monoidal/site flatness bridge comes from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. Substitute the two augmentation computations, scalar-balancing computation and constant-diagram computation into this ordinary equality; cancel their invertible computation maps. Naturality along the resolution and localization extensionality extend the augmentation equation to every derived object.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-pullback-compatibility] to the chosen normalized balancing on U and V. Assemble this pullback record with the scalar balancing, augmented units and constant-restriction comparison already constructed. The root conclusion has its original statement.

split_report.summary: Reused the existing common-quotient strict-tower comparison instead of introducing duplicates. Verified the common quotients and flatness, computed both reductions by one K-flat representative on the diagram site, proved the strict augmentation equation, and checked the normalized pullback equation on pure tensors before localization. No statement change and no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: lemma-weil-pbc-completed-exchange-coherence.proof.md, second paragraph: coefficient reduction is natural in tower transitions and uses the same conjugations. The seven steps supply the strict scalar-balancing and pullback normalization needed by that assertion.

tool_uses.why: General flat-term K-flat resolution existence on arbitrary small ringed sites, including the strict diagram site; no replacement of the unit proper-base-change route.
General K-flat computation and quasi-isomorphism invariance for scalar extension, applied to the two maps of ring sheaves on the small diagram site.

Canonical identification of the inverse image of the constant ring sheaf of A (not finite, so lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image does not give it) with the constant ring sheaf, carrying constants to constants; needed for the constant-coefficient side G_u and for the hypothesis a_U c_R = c_S u^{-1} a_V of lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction. Already used in this unit by lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison.

The delivery is 7 steps with 0 new nodes, and the statement is unchanged. I read every cited statement and did not find a false step. Step 1: the common-quotient hypotheses come from constant-exact (the cokernel of A^e→A gives image I^n·R) and from constant-completion-equivalence (flatness and A_T/I^n ≅ P_n, matching Stacks 093M at sites-modules.tex:8261). Step 3: the direction of ρ is the inverse of the common-quotient comparison. p⊗s ↦ p⊗s holds because both sides are identified with P/J_nP and s is locally r·1. The augmentation equation holds at chain level. Step 4: the datum requires P_n to be finite as a set, so the profinite node applies. Pullback along the coefficient isomorphisms is exact. Step 5: Q_V is not flat; the step handles this with a K-flat resolution and exact u^*. Step 6: I re-did the pure-tensor chase; both sides give u^{-1}(p⊗_R s), and differentials and transitions agree. Step 7: the maps descend through the site-derived-tensor-descent equivalence. Edge cases I=0, I=A, identity u and n=1 are fine. The closure has no cycle, no trf node, no SGA source and no dropped node. Overlap with pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison and constant-completion-equivalence is advisory only. (2) Step 2 used levelwise tensor on the diagram site without a citation; I named evaluation as the inverse image along e_n and cited lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison. proof_deps is recomputed.
